    "Implement stream resource cleanup as lifecycle hooks attached to the stream definition's deploy/destroy operations, leveraging the existing MessageBus SPI to query and delete queues/topics.",
    "Implement stream edit (U3) as an update-in-place operation that diffs current and desired properties and re-issues only the module-level changes, avoiding a full destroy/redeploy when possible.",
    "Support manifest file loading (U4) via a standard YAML format (Spring Boot-compatible) parsed using SnakeYAML, with inline --properties taking precedence over file values.",
    "Implement module tracing (U6) by re-using Spring Integration's existing global wiretap pattern (channel-global-wiretap), with property keys resolved via wildcard expansion (module.*.trace).",
    "Implement side channels (U7) as first-class named MessageBus channels declared in module definitions, exposed via a ChannelRegistry SPI so taps and external publishers can bind to them.",
    "Deliver the reference architectures (U5) as a set of runnable Maven-based sample projects (POC templates) accompanied by architectural documentation, not as production-ready deployments.",
    "Implement the taxi trips sample (U8) as a self-contained Spring XD stream definition plus a small custom module that performs windowed aggregations on the DEBS 2015 dataset.",
    "Reuse the existing XD test harness (xd-test) and the in-memory/integration-test MessageBus for unit and integration tests; no new test infrastructure is built."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The developer is a senior Java/Spring engineer with working knowledge of Spring XD internals (Module SPI, MessageBus SPI, stream deployment lifecycle).",

    "A single work product owner-style developer performs all activities sequentially; no parallel work or team coordination overhead is included.",
    "A work day equals 8 productive hours; calendar time is not the constraint.",
    "Underlying message broker (e.g., RabbitMQ) provides APIs sufficient to enumerate and delete the queues and topics the stream created.",

      "activity_id": "A1",

Includes detection of stale resources left by previous crashed deployments.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Stream edit capability (U3)",
      "activity_description": "Add an 'stream update' command (REST + shell) that accepts new deployment properties, computes a diff against the currently deployed definition, and applies only changed module properties without destroying the stream. Handle both deployed and undeployed states.",
      "most_likely_effort": 7.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Deployment manifest from file (U4)",
      "activity_description": "Extend the stream create/deploy commands to accept a --manifest option pointing to a YAML file; parse the file with SnakeYAML, merge its properties with any inline --properties (inline wins), and pass the combined map through the existing deploy path.",
      "most_likely_effort": 3.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Reference architectures on Spring XD (U5)",
      "activity_description": "Identify 2-3 representative XD domain scenarios (e.g., real-time analytics, data ingestion, ETL); create runnable Maven-based POC projects for each and write concise architecture-overview documentation describing components, message flows, and extension points.",

Document the property syntax.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Optional side channels (U7)",
      "activity_description": "Introduce a side-channel declaration in module metadata so non-primary channels (input/output) can be created on the bus at deploy time; expose a ChannelRegistry so module code and external taps can publish or subscribe to these named channels for tracing/observability.",
      "most_likely_effort": 5.0
    },

      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Taxi trips reference sample for DEBS 2015 (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Build a runnable Spring XD sample that ingests the NYC taxi trip event stream, applies a sliding-window aggregation (e.g., frequent routes / average fare over time windows), and writes results to a sink module. Include a README with run instructions.",

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement stream resource cleanup as lifecycle hooks attached to the stream definition's deploy/destroy operations, leveraging the existing MessageBus SPI to query and delete queues/topics.
Implement stream edit (U3) as an update-in-place operation that diffs current and desired properties and re-issues only the module-level changes, avoiding a full destroy/redeploy when possible.
Support manifest file loading (U4) via a standard YAML format (Spring Boot-compatible) parsed using SnakeYAML, with inline --properties taking precedence over file values.
Implement module tracing (U6) by re-using Spring Integration's existing global wiretap pattern (channel-global-wiretap), with property keys resolved via wildcard expansion (module.*.trace).
Implement side channels (U7) as first-class named MessageBus channels declared in module definitions, exposed via a ChannelRegistry SPI so taps and external publishers can bind to them.
Deliver the reference architectures (U5) as a set of runnable Maven-based sample projects (POC templates) accompanied by architectural documentation, not as production-ready deployments.
Implement the taxi trips sample (U8) as a self-contained Spring XD stream definition plus a small custom module that performs windowed aggregations on the DEBS 2015 dataset.
Reuse the existing XD test harness (xd-test) and the in-memory/integration-test MessageBus for unit and integration tests; no new test infrastructure is built.
assumptions: The developer is a senior Java/Spring engineer with working knowledge of Spring XD internals (Module SPI, MessageBus SPI, stream deployment lifecycle).
Spring XD source code is available, buildable, and the developer is familiar with the relevant modules (stream, deployer, messagebus).
A single work product owner-style developer performs all activities sequentially; no parallel work or team coordination overhead is included.
A work day equals 8 productive hours; calendar time is not the constraint.
Underlying message broker (e.g., RabbitMQ) provides APIs sufficient to enumerate and delete the queues and topics the stream created.
Java 8+ is the runtime, matching the Spring XD era; no JDK upgrade or migration work is in scope.
No new UI work is required — all features are exposed through the existing xd:> shell DSL and REST API surface.
Module property resolution and wildcard expansion logic already exists in XD's deployment code and only needs to be extended for the new 'trace' property.
The DEBS 2015 NYC taxi trip dataset is publicly downloadable and the sample can reference it as an external resource (no large dataset shipping).
No production hardening, security review, performance tuning, or back-porting to older Spring versions is in scope.
Documentation updates are limited to the new features; existing XD reference docs are not rewritten.

activities.activity_description: Review all 8 user stories, study the existing XD stream lifecycle, MessageBus SPI, and module property resolution; produce a short design note covering cleanup hooks, edit semantics, manifest format, tracing via wiretap, side-channel SPI, and the two deliverables (reference archs, taxi sample).

activities.activity_name: Stream resource cleanup on destroy (U1, U2)
activities.activity_description: Track all queues/topics created during stream deployment in the stream definition metadata, expose a stale-resource detector, and hook them into the destroy path so they are removed via the MessageBus SPI. Includes detection of stale resources left by previous crashed deployments.

Add an 'stream update' command (REST + shell) that accepts new deployment properties, computes a diff against the currently deployed definition, and applies only changed module properties without destroying the stream. Handle both deployed and undeployed states.

Extend the stream create/deploy commands to accept a --manifest option pointing to a YAML file; parse the file with SnakeYAML, merge its properties with any inline --properties (inline wins), and pass the combined map through the existing deploy path.

Identify 2-3 representative XD domain scenarios (e.g., real-time analytics, data ingestion, ETL); create runnable Maven-based POC projects for each and write concise architecture-overview documentation describing components, message flows, and extension points.

activities.activity_name: Module tracing via inline deployment properties (U6)
activities.activity_description: Recognize 'module.<name>.trace' / 'module.*.trace' deployment properties, expand wildcards against the deployed module set, and wire a Spring Integration global wiretap on the named module's output channel that logs/notifies per message. Document the property syntax.

Introduce a side-channel declaration in module metadata so non-primary channels (input/output) can be created on the bus at deploy time; expose a ChannelRegistry so module code and external taps can publish or subscribe to these named channels for tracing/observability.

activities.activity_name: Taxi trips reference sample for DEBS 2015 (U8)
